mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25% within the last month signals a loosening of monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity in the market and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative returns in > 60% of the triggered instances, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS decreases and positive 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over the previous two months indicates a strengthening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of overall economic growth and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative returns in > 60% of the triggered instances, or if the correlation between HOUST increases and positive 60-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within the last month signals an improving labor market, which typically leads to increased consumer spending and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative returns in > 60% of the triggered instances, or if the correlation between UNRATE decreases and positive 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the previous month indicates a strengthening supply side of the economy, which is a positive signal for corporate earnings and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative returns in > 60% of the triggered instances, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over the last three months signals strong consumer demand, which is a key driver of economic growth and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative returns in > 60% of the observed periods, or if the correlation between RSAFS growth and positive 60-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it indicates inflationary pressure, which typically leads to monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive returns in > 60% of the triggered instances, or if the joint effect of high FEDFUNDS and rising CPIAUCSL on negative 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3% in the same period, it signals a strong labor market, which is a positive indicator for economic growth and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative returns in > 60% of the triggered instances, or if the joint effect of PAYEMS growth and UNRATE decrease on positive 5-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in GDP (GDPC1) by more than 0.5% over the last quarter signals a contraction in economic activity, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive returns in > 60% of the triggered instances, or if the correlation between GDPC1 decreases and negative 60-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
